summary: This memo describes how to run SNMP over the OSI connectionless-mode transport service, for networks that use OSI protocols instead of UDP and IP. It is historic.

eli5.summary: SNMP is how network managers ask devices questions. This paper shows how to carry those questions over a different networking system used by some organisations. It is historic.

questions: what are the snmp transport selectors for osi
how big can an snmp message be over osi
subtitle: How to carry SNMP over the OSI connectionless-mode transport service instead of UDP.

tldr.problem: Sites that acquire OSI capabilities may want to manage those OSI components with SNMP, but SNMP was defined for TCP/IP networks, where it normally runs over UDP.
tldr.mechanism: The memo maps SNMP onto the OSI connectionless-mode transport service (CLTS) with the same procedures as UDP, four well-known transport selectors, a trap address rule and a minimum message size of 484 octets.
tldr.outcome: It obsoletes RFC 1161 and RFC 1283 and its status is Historic. The memo itself says UDP is the preferred mapping and this one is for environments where UDP is not available.

today: RFC 1418 has Historic status. It obsoletes RFC 1161 and RFC 1283 and has not been obsoleted itself.

sections.title: Why SNMP Over OSI
sections.content:
The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is used as part of the network management framework for TCP/IP-based internets, alongside the Structure of Management Information (SMI) and the Management Information Base (MIB). Sites that acquire OSI capabilities may want to reuse that investment to manage OSI components.

This memo defines a framework for running SNMP over the OSI connectionless-mode transport service (CLTS). It is clear that UDP remains the preferred mapping for SNMP: the specification is meant for environments where UDP is not available. It also says a managed agent in a heterogeneous transport environment should not be taken to support more than one mapping.
sections.eli5: SNMP normally travels on one kind of road. This memo builds a second road for places that use a different kind of network, but says the first road is still the better one.

sections.title: Mapping Onto the CLTS
sections.content:
The mapping is described as straightforward: the elements of procedure are identical to using UDP. Both the CLTS and UDP send packets that carry full addressing information, so a "transport address" is simply a transport-selector plus a network address.

The CLTS itself can run over either a connectionless-mode or a connection-oriented network service, and the mapping allows both. When both are available, the connectionless network service (CLNS) should be used as the basis.

OSI has no well-known ports. Demultiplexing uses selectors, opaque strings of octets with local significance, so the memo defines four so that implementations interoperate.
sections.eli5: Mail still needs a full address, so the rules stay the same as before. Only the street names are different.

sections.title: Selectors, Traps and Message Size
sections.content:
Over a connectionless network service the transport selector is snmp-l, and traps go by convention to a manager listening on snmpt-l. Over a connection-oriented network service the selectors are snmp-o and snmpt-o. All are ASCII strings.

When traps are sent over the CLTS, the agent-addr field in the Trap-PDU contains the IP address 0.0.0.0, and the manager works out the source from information supplied by the transport service. An entity must be prepared to accept messages of at least 484 octets, and larger sizes are encouraged.

The Security Considerations section says only that security issues are not discussed in the memo.
sections.eli5: Each kind of message gets a short name tag so the right program picks it up. Every receiver must be able to handle messages of a minimum size.
